title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Liu Z, Liu Y, Li S, Zhang X, Qiang R, Jin F, Guo L, Hou T
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Since surgery can only remove lesions of a larger size visible to the naked eye, the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery is high. In recent years, numerous scholars have found that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment is effective in reducing the recurrence rate of postoperative fibroids, as well as improving the clinical treatment rate, regulating serum hormone levels, reducing plasma viscosity, and promoting the restoration of uterine volume following surgery. Several randomized controlled trials have been undertaken on the prevention and treatment of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids using patented Chinese medicines and self-proposed formulations, such as Guizhi Fuling Pill, Xiaozheng decoction, Xiangleng pill, Zhengjia decoction, Xiaoliu decoction, Guizhi Jiliu pill, Huoxue Huayu formula, Huoxue Xiaozheng decoction, Shugan Sanjie decoction, Gongliuxiao capsule, Hongjin Xiaojie concentrated pill, and Jiawei Guizhi Fuling decoction. However, no study has systematically evaluated Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) in reducing the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of CHM for the prevention of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids, evaluating its efficacy and safety. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted on PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Information Database (VIP), WanFang Database, and China Biomedical Database (CBM) to identify randomized controlled clinical studies conducted up to March 2025 that examined the efficacy of CHM in treating patients with postoperative uterine fibroids. Two institutes were independently under-selected, and data were extracted and quality assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software 5.4, and forest plots were generated. The quality of evidence was assessed using GRADEpro 3.2.2. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000288). RESULTS: 16 trials were included in this study, and the postoperative recurrence rate after treatment was mainly analyzed. CHM treatment reduces postoperative recurrence rates in patients with uterine fibroids compared to the blank (6 trials, n = 588; OR (odds ratio) = 0.22; 95 % CI (95 % confidence intervals) = 0.14-0.34; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001), conventional western medicine (CWM) (1 trial, n = 80; OR = 0.30; 95 % CI = 0.09-0.93, p = 0.04), and combined CHM with CWM (9 trials, n = 959; OR = 0.29; 95 % CI = 0.19-0.46; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001). In addition, CHM is also effective in improving clinical efficiency, restoring serum sex hormone levels, lowering plasma viscosity, and reducing uterine volume. CHM is generally considered safe, with a low incidence of adverse reactions. CONCLUSION: CHM is effective in avoiding recurrence of uterine fibroids after surgery, excelling in terms of overall effectiveness, restoring female hormone levels, improving hemorheological indices, and promoting uterine recovery and safety. However, these findings are preliminary and still need to be validated by higher-quality studies.

title: Effect of lung transplantation on biventricular function in pulmonary arterial hypertension: A systematic review.
authors: Mohammed AS, Gurram P, Mellacheruvu SP, Lekkala SP, Takagi MA, Kanagala SG, Yasmeen U, Lababidi H
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) leads to progressive right ventricular (RV) failure and secondary left ventricular (LV) dysfunction due to chronic pressure overload and ventricular interdependence. Lung transplantation (LTx) is an established treatment for end-stage PAH, yet patterns of biventricular recovery and the role of veno-arterial perioperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) remain incompletely defined. A PubMed search identified studies published from 1990 to 2025 using MeSH terms related to lung transplantation, ventricular function, echocardiography, cardiac MRI, and ECMO. Prospective studies, retrospective analyses, and case series evaluating post-transplant cardiac function in PAH were included. A total of 13 studies were included. Across studies, LTx resulted in rapid and substantial RV reverse remodeling, with improvements in RV size, mass, systolic function, tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary pressures. This reduction in RV afterload was accompanied by progressive improvement of RV output. In contrast, LV recovery was more variable, possibly due to chronic underfilling and LV remodeling. Cardiac MRI and echocardiography demonstrated progressive biventricular structural and functional adaptation over time. Perioperative VA-ECMO may provide hemodynamic support during this transition by unloading the RV and maintaining perfusion while ventricular loading conditions rapidly change. Lung transplantation for PAH initiates transition from chronic RV pressure overload and LV underfilling to improved pulmonary vascular conditions and subsequent biventricular recovery. Further longitudinal studies are needed to identify predictors of maladaptive LV responses and determine which patients may benefit from prolonged perioperative VA-ECMO support.

title: Thyroid biomarker biosensing: Nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical platforms, clinical translation, point-of-care technologies, and intelligent diagnostics.
authors: Bathinapatla A, Pakrudheen I, Kanchi S
abstract: Thyroid disorders represent a substantial clinical burden, requiring reliable biomarker measurement for diagnosis, monitoring, and disease assessment. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), thyroglobulin (Tg), calcitonin (CT), and thyroid-associated nucleic acid biomarkers are important analytical targets. Although established immunoassays, ELISA, imaging, and cytological methods remain integral to clinical practice, limitations related to laboratory infrastructure, sample requirements, and workflow complexity have driven the development of alternative analytical platforms. This review focuses primarily on nanomaterial-assisted electrochemical biosensors for thyroid biomarker analysis, examining how nanomaterial properties, biorecognition strategies, and electrochemical transduction influence analytical performance. Metal and metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon nanomaterials, metal-organic frameworks, metal chalcogenides, MXenes, quantum dots, and molecularly imprinted polymers are discussed for their roles in signal amplification, interfacial charge transfer, selectivity, and sensor stability. Complementary approaches, including chemiluminescent, photoelectrochemical, optical, and other emerging sensing strategies, are also considered to contextualize the broader analytical landscape, particularly in relation to their implementation in commercial laboratory and point-of-care platforms for thyroid analysis. Seventy representative analytical and diagnostic systems are comparatively evaluated according to sensing technology, detection range, sample type, and assay time, together with their progression toward portable point-of-care devices, commercial analyzers, rapid diagnostic formats, and wearable platforms. Emerging artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for signal interpretation, disease classification, and risk assessment are discussed. Challenges in nanomaterial reproducibility, bioreceptor stability, biofouling, matrix effects, fabrication, analytical standardization, external validation, and clinical translation are critically examined. The review identifies key analytical and technological priorities for translating thyroid biosensors from sensitive experimental platforms into robust, reproducible, and clinically relevant diagnostic tools.

title: Next-generation hyphenated analytical technologies in natural product research: From high-resolution separation and structural elucidation to dereplication, metabolomics and drug discovery.
authors: Dar AA, Mukhtar M, Shameem SA, Singh N
abstract: Natural products occupy a unique position at the interface of chemistry, biology and medicine and continue to provide structurally diverse molecules for drug discovery, chemical biology, nutrition and therapeutic development. Their investigation, however, is complicated by the enormous chemical complexity of natural-product extracts, the presence of structurally related metabolites, isomeric and isobaric compounds, wide concentration ranges, matrix effects and the frequent occurrence of previously uncharacterized constituents. Over the past decade, advances in chromatographic separation, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS), ion mobility spectrometry (IMS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and computational analysis have fundamentally changed how these challenges are addressed. High performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS), HPLC-MS/MS, HPLC-NMR, LC-solid-phase extraction (SPE)-NMR and capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry (CE-MS) have evolved from individual hyphenated techniques into integrated analytical workflows capable of linking chemical separation with molecular characterization, dereplication and biological prioritization. In parallel, molecular networking, spectral databases, in silico fragmentation, machine learning and metabolomics platforms have transformed the interpretation of increasingly complex datasets. This review critically examines these developments, emphasizing the complementary information generated by chromatographic, MS and NMR measurements and their integration with computational approaches. Particular attention is given to HRMS/MS, data-independent acquisition, ion mobility, LC-SPE-NMR, molecular networking, spectral-library searching, metabolite annotation confidence and emerging artificial-intelligence-assisted workflows. The review argues that the principal transformation in natural-product analysis is not simply improved instrumental sensitivity, but the emergence of multidimensional and computationally integrated workflows that connect extraction, separation, detection, structural annotation, dereplication, metabolomics and bioactivity-guided discovery. Remaining challenges including incomplete databases, isomer discrimination, annotation uncertainty, reproducibility and the need for orthogonal structure confirmation are discussed, together with future opportunities for automated, multidimensional and FAIR-data-enabled natural-product discovery.

title: Next-generation analytical platforms for neurochemical sensing: from conventional biosensors to intelligent brain interfaces.
authors: Ardah MT, Kubaev A, Patel JR, Saxena R, Mutee AF, Al-Hussein MA, Sharma C, Shayesteh OH
abstract: Neurochemical sensing is central to understanding brain function, neurological disorders, and precision neurotherapeutics. Despite advances in electrochemical, optical, implantable, wearable, and genetically encoded technologies, current platforms remain limited by molecular selectivity, long-term stability, biofouling, complex data interpretation, and clinical translation. This review critically examines 83 representative studies encompassing nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical sensors, implantable and wearable devices, genetically encoded and CRISPR-engineered systems, AI-assisted analytical frameworks, and multimodal bioelectronic interfaces. Among the reviewed platforms, 68.7% were based on electrochemical or electrical sensing, whereas only 9.6% incorporated explicit AI/ML-assisted data analysis, indicating that intelligent analytical functionalities remain relatively limited. AI-assisted platforms have shown promising capabilities for signal discrimination, quantitative analysis, and enhanced analytical performance across diverse neurochemical sensing modalities, but their reported performance remains highly dependent on the sensing architecture, experimental conditions, and level of validation. Rather than providing a conventional technology-centered survey, this review establishes a unified framework for evaluating neurochemical sensing across five dimensions: molecular selectivity, spatiotemporal resolution, operational stability, intelligent data interpretation, and translational readiness. The reviewed evidence indicates a transition from conventional single-modality sensing toward integrated platforms incorporating multimodal detection and intelligent data interpretation, with adaptive and closed-loop interfacing emerging as future directions. By connecting advances in molecular recognition, functional materials, bioelectronics, and AI, this review identifies key design principles, persistent bottlenecks, and realistic priorities for translating next-generation neurochemical sensing platforms into reliable and clinically relevant intelligent interfaces.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Thoracoabdominal Trauma in Disaster.
authors: Morrissey S, Chung T
journal: The Surgical clinics of North America
abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents overwhelm resources and force deviations from conventional care. Thoracoabdominal trauma involves 2 unforgiving compartments in which exsanguination, tension physiology, tamponade, and contamination are rapidly lethal. This article reviews the operational management of thoracic and abdominal injury when volume, personnel, and blood products are constrained. Topics include rapid recognition and decompression of tension pneumothorax, massive hemothorax, and cardiac tamponade; indications for damage control thoracic surgery, thoracic packing, temporary closure, and vascular shunting; hemorrhage and contamination control by retroperitoneal zone; and temporary abdominal closure options. Emphasis is placed on triage, resource stewardship, and deferring definitive reconstruction.

title: Critical Care Management of Disaster-Related Organ Failure.
authors: Hertel K, Bard M
journal: The Surgical clinics of North America
abstract: Disasters generate high volumes of multisystem trauma while simultaneously degrading the staff, equipment, and electricity that critical care depends on. This article reviews management of disaster-related organ failure under resource constraint. It outlines step-wise respiratory support, from high-flow nasal cannula and noninvasive ventilation to lung-protective mechanical ventilation; prevention and treatment of acute kidney injury (AKI), including dialysis options for AKI and end-stage renal disease patients; recognition of hemorrhagic, neurogenic, cardiogenic, and obstructive shock; and secondary complications including coagulopathy, hypothermia, abdominal compartment syndrome, hepatic dysfunction, and hyperglycemia. Ethical triage, palliation, telecritical care, and staffing models are also addressed.

title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
authors: Kirkpatrick S, Khan U
journal: The Surgical clinics of North America
abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: Serrated Pathway-Related Post-Colonoscopy Colorectal Cancer　Detected During Surveillance Colonoscopy: A Case Report.
authors: Hadatsuki H, Ichijima R, Mizuguchi Y, Toyoshima N, Okita H, Haga T, Kumamoto Y, Tsukamoto S
abstract: Post-colonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains a critical clinical challenge, and sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) are important precursor lesions. We report a case of advanced transverse colon cancer suspected to be associated with the serrated pathway that was detected during periodic surveillance colonoscopy. An 82-year-old male had undergone periodic surveillance colonoscopy after curative resection via endoscopic submucosal dissection for rectosigmoid intramucosal cancer. Colonoscopy revealed a type 2 advanced tumor near the hepatic flexure and multiple serrated lesions throughout the colon, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for serrated polyposis syndrome (SPS). Immunohistochemistry showed deficient mismatch repair with loss of MLH1 and PMS2, and molecular analysis revealed BRAF V600E and KRAS mutations. The patient underwent robot-assisted transverse colectomy, and pathological staging was pT3N0. He remains recurrence-free 6 months after surgery. This case highlights the difficulty of distinguishing between a missed serrated lesion and a newly developed cancer in serrated pathway-related PCCRC. In patients with multiple SSLs or SPS, high-quality colonoscopy, recognition of SPS criteria, complete resection of detectable serrated lesions, and individualized surveillance strategies may be essential for the prevention and early detection of PCCRC.

title: Facile synthesis of a novel fluorescent Au nanoclusters using sunset yellow as template and their application in multiple substances detection.
authors: Li D, Zhang X, Liu X, Song X, Wang Y
abstract: Fluorescent (FL) Au nanoclusters (Au NCs) have excellent physicochemical properties and been widely used in analysis fields. In this study, a novel FL Au NCs with dual excitation wavelength and dual emission wavelength was prepared by a one-pot aqueous method. Sunset yellow (SY) was firstly used as ligand to fabricate Au NCs and the synthetic method is extremely facile. The FL performance of SY-Au NCs is sensitive to pH, oxidizing/reducing substances and Hg2+. The FL response mechanism is different and the details were discussed. The detection limits of SY-Au NCs for NaClO, ascorbic acid (AA) and Hg2+ are 200 μM, 0.5 μM and 50 nM, respectively. The spiked experiment in real samples reflects the potential of probe for preliminary Hg2+ screening in drinking water.

title: A dithioacetal-based NIR fluorescent chemosensor for Hg2+ detection in biological and environmental samples.
authors: Wan J, Li W, Chen M, Wang Y, Yang X, Zhu M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: The widespread occurrence, high toxicity, and bioaccumulative nature of mercury (Hg2+) render its pollution a critical concern for ecosystems and human well-being. Hence, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent chemosensor (DHDM) was constructed through a naphthyl-substituted dicyanoisophorone dye and a 1,2-ethanedithiol recognition unit, which responds via a Hg2+-induced specific cleavage reaction and an ICT mechanism. DHDM exhibits excellent analytical performance, including a large stokes shift (192 nm), ultrafast reaction time (<1 min), sensitive detection limit (0.93 μg/L), which is significantly lower than the requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's drinking water guideline standards. DHDM also exhibits high selectivity and robust anti-interference capability when challenged with various competing metal ions and amino acids. Such performance originates from the Hg2+-promoted deprotection of the dithioacetal moiety, which reinstates the conjugated fluorophore. The proposed reaction pathway has been corroborated by 1H NMR, HRMS, and DFT calculations. Meanwhile, DHDM successfully enabled in situ imaging of Hg2+ in HeLa cells, zebrafish, and germinating plant seeds, demonstrating good biocompatibility and tissue penetration, and yielding reliable recovery rates (89-109%) in spiked environmental water samples. Overall, the study establishes a reliable tool for mercury monitoring and constructs a multifunctional molecular scaffold, providing new perspectives for the rational design of advanced fluorescent chemosensors to address various challenges in the environmental and biomedical fields.

title: Effects of auxiliary acceptors on two-photon absorption and intramolecular charge transfer of D1-D-Ai-π-A hydrazone derivatives.
authors: Wang W, Chen M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Hydrazone derivatives have recently emerged as promising candidates for two-photon absorption (TPA) materials due to their tunable donor-acceptor architectures and excellent nonlinear optical responses. Herein, the one-photon absorption (OPA), TPA, and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) of four novel D1-D-Ai-π-A hydrazone derivatives modified with a planar trithiophene moiety are calculated using density functional theory and the sum-over-states method to study the effects of auxiliary acceptors Ai on the absorption spectra and the corresponding photoinduced ICT mechanisms. The computational results show that the stronger electron-withdrawing Ai group exhibits a red-shifted OPA maximum but reduces OPA intensity due to enhanced orbital separation. For the TPA, the derivative with a moderate electron-withdrawing Ai exhibits the largest cross-section, as it maintains balanced electron delocalization and efficient two-step charge reorganization, whereas an excessively strong electron-withdrawing acceptor induces localized charge recombination that suppresses TPA efficiency. The ICT analysis reveals that although strong electron-withdrawing acceptors enlarge electron-hole separation, overly strong withdrawal hinders long-range transfer. This work provides a design guideline for developing high-performance optical limiting materials based on hydrazone derivatives, and the underlying principle may offer useful insight for the design of other donor-π-acceptor systems.

title: Genetically engineered extracellular vesicles with chimeric antigen receptors of human stem cell-derived neutrophils targeting fibroblast activation protein to modulate tumor microenvironment.
authors: Esmonde C, Sun L, Jin G, Michaelides L, Syed F, Bhattarai J, Driscoll T, Quiñones-Hinojosa A
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most commonly occurring central nervous system tumor, accounting for over 50% of gliomas, with a poor survival rate. A primary driver of GBM progression is the fibrotic stroma, where excess extracellular matrix deposition creates a dense network that excludes immune cells and chemotherapeutic agents. While targeting tumor-associated fibroblasts (TAFs) via fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cells is a promising strategy, off-target toxicities limit the clinical utility of the treatment. To address these safety concerns, extracellular vesicles (EVs) of FAP-CAR-engineered neutrophils differentiated from human pluripotent stem cells were isolated and characterized, including proteomic profile, microRNA content, in vitro bioactivity, and in vivo biodistribution in this study. Multi-omic profiling revealed that CAR engineering enriched EVs with proinflammatory proteins, iron-transferring proteins, and proliferation regulators, and a significant upregulation of miRNAs targeting FAP and proliferation-regulating genes was observed. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that these EVs are selectively cytotoxic to TAFs, reducing the expression of BCL-2 and RAS-MAPK-ERK signaling pathway genes. These EVs also demonstrated cytotoxicity to patient-derived GBM spheroids. Furthermore, in vivo biodistribution results confirmed that FAP-CAR EVs are capable of systemic circulation and payload delivery, showing a significant increase in accumulation within the liver and spleen compared to free Cy5.5. These findings suggest that CAR engineering enhances the ability of FAP-CAR EVs to inhibit TAF proliferation and induce apoptosis. FAP-targeting CAR EVs are positioned as a targeted bioengineered delivery platform with the potential for remodeling the tumor microenvironment and slowing the progression of desmoplasia in GBM.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Liquid contactable colorimetric sensor array for bacteria discrimination.
authors: Kim YM, Lee MG, Kim SH, Shin DI, Lee JH, Kim J, Lim SH, Yi GR
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of bacterial metabolites in liquid culture is critical for early diagnosis of sepsis, yet conventional dye-based colorimetric sensor arrays (CSAs) are hindered by dye leaching and poor interfacial interactions in aqueous environments. Here, we introduce a polydimethylsiloxane-based CSA (PDMS-CSA) platform that overcomes these limitations by leveraging the intrinsic hydrophobicity of PDMS to stably immobilize water-soluble indicator dyes within the polymer matrix. This design ensures direct, unimpeded contact between analytes and sensors, enhancing both sensitivity and reproducibility. The PDMS matrix further contributes by preventing dye leaching while facilitating mass transport of bacterial metabolites such as ammonia (500 μM), hydrogen sulfide (50 μM), and carbon dioxide (1.7 mM) to the immobilized indicators, thereby enabling rapid and robust colorimetric responses. Using this platform, we achieved reliable differentiation between cocci and bacilli within 3 h, demonstrating a capability for rapid, clinically relevant bacterial identification. By combining operational simplicity with high analytical performance in complex liquid media, PDMS-CSAs represent a transformative approach for point-of-care sepsis diagnostics. Beyond sepsis, this strategy offers a versatile framework for the development of next-generation, non-invasive microbial sensor operating platforms with broad translational potential in clinical and environmental monitoring.

title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Tan W, Wang C, Liu X, Deng J, Sang Z, Hu X
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR. RESULTS: BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice. CONCLUSION: BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

title: Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization.
authors: Huo W, Hou X, Huang Y, Li Z, Chen X, Feng J, Kong Y, Pan S
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI) has high mortality and limited therapies. Tao-He-Cheng-Qi decoction protects against sepsis-associated acute lung injury by modulating gut microbiota and succinate-associated pulmonary macrophage polarization. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the protective effects of THCQ pretreatment against LPS-induced SA-ALI and examine associated changes in gut microbiota, succinate levels, SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling and macrophage polarization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A murine SA-ALI model was induced by intraperitoneal LPS. Lung injury, inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α), and M1/M2 polarization were assessed. Gut microbiota was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing. Succinate levels, SUCNR1, and PKA-CREB signaling were measured. Microbiota dependence was tested using antibiotic depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from THCQ-treated donors, exogenous succinate, and macrophage depletion with clodronate liposomes. RESULTS: THCQ pretreatment attenuated lung injury, reduced IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and shifted pulmonary macrophage polarization toward an M2-like phenotype. These effects were accompanied by altered gut microbiota composition, a lower abundance ratio of bacterial families grouped in the exploratory succinate-metabolism analysis, reduced serum and pulmonary succinate levels, lower SUCNR1 expression, and increased PKA/CREB phosphorylation. Antibiotic treatment attenuated the protective responses to THCQ, while FMT from THCQ-treated donors reproduced improvements in lung injury. Exogenous succinate attenuated THCQ-mediated protection. Clo-Lipo treatment reduced the proportions of alveolar and interstitial macrophages and markedly attenuated the protective effects of THCQ. CONCLUSION: THCQ treatment protects against SA-ALI and suppresses M1-like macrophage polarization. These effects are accompanied by changes in gut microbiota composition, reduced succinate levels, and altered SUCNR1-PKA-CREB signaling. Together, the findings support a role for gut microbiota-metabolism-immune interactions in the protective effects of THCQ.

title: Defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerfaces enable ultrasound-amplified built-in electric fields for bacterial envelope destabilization and implant infection control.
authors: Liu P, Lu S, Chen J, Cheng H, Yan J, Yao X, Wang G, Zhang X
abstract: Built-in electric fields (BIEFs) at piezoelectric heterointerfaces are widely invoked to assist charge separation, but their contribution to antibacterial activity under ultrasound remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerface strategy to investigate BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects. Density functional theory (DFT)-guided screening identifies a dual-vacancy piezoelectric heterojunction (BTO3-X/MoS2-X) with enhanced interfacial polarization. Under ultrasound, BTO3-X/MoS2-X efficiently kills Staphylococcus aureus, accompanied by pronounced bacterial envelope destabilization. This response is accompanied by membrane lipid perturbation, increased permeability, respiratory inhibition, and intracellular ROS accumulation. GROMACS simulations show that a model lipid bilayer destabilizes only under a sufficiently strong applied electric field. In infected implant models, ultrasound activated BTO3-X/MoS2-X reduces early peri-implant bacterial burden and promotes a repair-favorable inflammatory microenvironment. These findings highlight the potential contribution of BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects to ultrasound responsive antibacterial activity and offer a defect-engineering strategy for implant infection control.

title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
authors: Wang Z, Su Y, Zhang S, Yu B, Wei Y, Liu H, Veselova IA, Lv S
abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8+ T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: HaloTag-directed magnetic immobilization of PAD4 for target-based screening of natural-product inhibitors.
authors: Xu H, Zhu D, Zhao Z, Zuo H, Wang Y, Fang Y, Li P, Mu Y
abstract: Target-directed screening of bioactive natural products is often limited by the instability, poor recoverability, and repeated preparation requirements of soluble recombinant enzymes. Here, we developed a reusable magnetic peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) screening platform based on site-directed HaloTag immobilization. Recombinant Halo-PAD4 was captured directly from crude lysate by chloroalkane-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs-Cl) without an additional labor-intensive and time-consuming enzyme purification step, generating MNPs-Halo-PAD4 with retained catalytic activity and inhibitor responsiveness. Compared with soluble PAD4, the immobilized enzyme showed improved activity retention during storage and temperature exposure and could be magnetically recovered for repeated assays. The platform was applied to screen water, 75% ethanol, and ethyl acetate extracts of 15 traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) materials. Among the tested materials, Alpinia officinarum consistently exhibited the strongest PAD4-inhibitory activity in both soluble and immobilized PAD4 assays. Activity-guided high-performance liquid chromatography fractionation localized the inhibitory activity to fraction F3. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry tentatively annotated 13 constituents, and authentic-standard testing prioritized galangin. Galangin inhibited PAD4 with an IC50 value of 46.6 μM and showed direct interaction with PAD4 by biolayer interferometry, with an apparent KD of 7.8 μM. Molecular docking further provided a structural hypothesis for the interaction. This workflow combines HaloTag-chloroalkane chemistry, magnetic enzyme immobilization, liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry for the screening of PAD4 inhibitors. This proposed one-step capture and immobilization of recombinant protein also supports ligand screening for other protein targets.

title: Au@Ag nanostar@ZIF-8 hydrogel composites: A flexible SERS platform with molecular sieving and high sensitivity.
authors: Liu L, Sun Y, Yin N, Zhang Y, Wu Y
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is a highly sensitive trace analysis technique that provides molecular fingerprint specificity, single-molecule detection capability, and non-destructive characterization. However, the application of conventional rigid SERS substrates in field-based in situ detection is severely constrained by their inherent inability to conform to complex surfaces and their insufficient molecular selectivity. This study reports a rationally engineered flexible SERS substrate comprising Au@Ag core-shell nanostars selectively functionalized with ZIF-8 at their tips (denoted Au@Ag NS@ZIF-8), which uniformly and stably immobilized within a three-dimensional porous chitosan hydrogel foam. The resulting substrate delivers an analytical enhancement factor of 2.03 × 107 for 4-aminophenylthiol (4-ATP), achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 10-9 M. Crucially, the ZIF-8 shells confer size-exclusive molecular sieving, thereby ensuring high selectivity toward target smaller analytes in complex matrices. In addition, the substrate exhibits excellent inter-batch reproducibility and spatial uniformity (RSD∼8.98%), and temporal stability after 60 days of ambient storage. This substrate enables synergistic optimization of sensitivity, selectivity, and stability, thereby providing a promising platform for rapid on-site screening of trace hazardous substances in food safety and environmental monitoring.

title: Environmental Impact of Conventional Versus Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Colorectal Lesions: A Procedure-Based Life Cycle Assessment With Pooled Effectiveness Estimates.
authors: Calabrese G, Moll F, Neves JAC, Bonacci L, Sinagra E, Castiglione F, Maida M, Albéniz-Arbizu E
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions. METHODS: In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO2-equivalent/procedure), waste, life-cycle water consumption, fossil resource scarcity, and terrestrial acidification. Exploratory GWP per en bloc resection was estimated using pooled randomized-trial and pilot-cohort data. RESULTS: Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.17 vs. 0.77 ± 0.20 m3; p < 0.001), fossil resource scarcity (0.33 ± 0.10 vs. 0.40 ± 0.09 kg oil-eq; p = 0.007), and terrestrial acidification (0.0052 ± 0.0018 vs. 0.0068 ± 0.0018 kg SO2-eq; p = 0.003). Findings were consistent across scenario and uncertainty analyses. In the meta-analysis-based model, GWP per en bloc resection was lower with U-EMR than EMR (2.59 vs. 3.51 kg CO2-eq), corresponding to a 26.3% relative reduction. CONCLUSIONS: U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: No. 165/26.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
authors: Xing Y, Gao Y, Hong Z, Tian C, Cai H, Chu H, Yang Y, Liang PY
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: Enrichment characteristics and hyperspectral quantitative retrieval of lithium and rare earth element concentrations in coal.
authors: Zhao H, Cheng S, Wang M, Zhao L, Li C, Sun S, Wei Y, Tian Y
abstract: Coal is a host of critical metals, and rapid, non-destructive quantification of these metals is important for resource assessment. This study investigated lithium (Li) and rare earth elements (REE) in coal samples from the Sihe Coal Mine, Shanxi Province, and the Hebi Coal Mine, Henan Province, China. Hyperspectral data (350-2500 nm) were processed using First-order Derivative (FD) and Continuum Removal (CR), followed by feature selection with Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS) and Boruta. Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), Back-Propagation Neural Networks (BPNN), and Particle Swarm Optimization-Support Vector Regression (PSO-SVR) were used to develop quantitative retrieval models. Lithium was relatively enriched, whereas REE concentration were generally within the normal range. The FD-Boruta-BPNN model achieved the highest prediction accuracy for both Li (R2=0.912) and REE (R2=0.968), using fewer input wavelengths. These findings demonstrate that spectral preprocessing, feature selection, and modeling algorithms jointly influence retrieval performance, highlighting the need to balance predictive accuracy and model complexity. Predictions likely rely on indirect spectral information associated with mineral carriers rather than direct elemental absorption features. However, the limited sample size and geographical coverage constrain generalizability. Future research should incorporate larger, independent datasets from diverse geological settings, verify spectral-response mechanisms through mineralogical analysis, and extend the framework to other coal-hosted critical metals and hyperspectral imaging.

title: Lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis and biomarker identification.
authors: Zhang H, Lin W, Pan H, Cao L, Wang Y, Sun H, Zhao Y, Jia Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA), a chronic, autoimmune form of arthritis that causes joint inflammation and occurs with the skin condition psoriasis, is difficult to clinically diagnose at an early stage due to insignificant symptoms and lack of biomarkers. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a powerful tool to identify specific biomolecules for liquid biopsy. Here, we establish a lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of PsA and identification of potential biomarkers. The fs-laser-nanofabricated Au@mica SERS substrates with a relative standard deviation of 8.80% in intensity homogeneity are employed to obtain reliable serum Raman spectra. The SVM algorithm is performed to train the machine-learning model for PsA classification using only 26 samples (PsA = 13 and healthy controls = 13). The hyperplane coefficient vectors from the trained SVM model are then employed as the filtered weights of Raman shifts, followed by logistic-probability mapping and Welch's t-test to filter highly-significant spectral features, identifying 432 most-significant Raman shifts for 7 potential biomarkers. The trained LiSVM-SERS model demonstrates the outstanding sensitivity and specificity of 98.0% and 96.0%, respectively, validated by an internal independent blind-test cohort (PsA = 30, healthy controls = 30) and a cross disease-control cohort (systemic lupus erythematosus = 15, rheumatoid arthritis = 15, and osteoarthritis = 15). The present work not only provides a simple and lightweight non-invasive technique to diagnose PsA, but also paves a new way to identify the potential biomarkers from the label-free serum SERS spectra for autoimmune disorders.

title: Spatial organization of magnetic nanoparticles in chitosan-gelatin hydrogels enables enhanced magnetic actuation and cell response under dynamic stimulation.
authors: Viteri A, Ginebra MP, García-Torres J
abstract: Magnetically responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for remotely modulating HFF-1 fibroblasts behavior through dynamic mechanical stimulation; however, the influence of magnetic nanoparticle spatial organization on magnetic actuation and cell response remains unexplored. Herein, we report the development of chitosan-gelatin magnetic hydrogels with controlled Fe3O4 nanoparticle distribution including homogeneously dispersed, and spatially patterned configurations, as a strategy to engineer localized mechanotransduction and magnetic actuation. The role of nanoparticle organization on the physicochemical, magnetic, and biological properties of the hydrogels has been analyzed. Structural characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of Fe3O4 nanoparticles while preserving their crystalline inverse spinel structure. Morphological and topographical analyses revealed that patterned hydrogels exhibit well-defined nanoparticle-rich and nanoparticle-free regions, generating pronounced microscale heterogeneity throughout the material. The incorporation and spatial confinement of Fe3O4 nanoparticles significantly influenced the hydrogel properties, increasing stiffness, reducing swelling capacity, and enhancing magnetic responsiveness. Notably, patterned hydrogels displayed higher saturation magnetization and magnetic susceptibility than homogeneously dispersed systems, indicating that nanoparticle confinement promotes cooperative magnetic interactions and more efficient magnetic actuation. Biological studies demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility for all hydrogel formulations. While static magnetic stimulation slightly reduced fibroblast proliferation, dynamic magnetic stimulation significantly enhanced cell proliferation, spreading, and cytoskeletal organization, particularly in patterned hydrogels. These effects are attributed to cyclic mechanical cues generated by amplified magnetic-to-mechanical transduction within the patterned magnetic domains. Overall, this study demonstrates that nanoparticle spatial organization is a key design parameter for engineering magnetically responsive hydrogels with tunable magnetic actuation and controllable cellular responses for tissue engineering applications.
